    Randomized Blocks: Crossed Mixed-Model Permutations

    randomized-block-crossed-permutation.Rmd

    This vignette demonstrates the exact Phase 7 permutation envelope: one fixed treatment randomized within every block, a random block intercept, an explicit treatment-by-block random component, and equal replicate observations in every cell.

    The community is simulated because the standard vegan datasets do not encode a complete replicated randomized-block experiment. Bray–Curtis distances are calculated with vegan::vegdist().

    Simulate a replicated block experiment 

    sampling <- expand.grid(
  quadrat = factor(1:3),
  treatment = factor(c("reference", "restored")),
  block = factor(1:8)
)
cell <- interaction(sampling$treatment, sampling$block, drop = TRUE)

set.seed(20260718)
species <- 12
baseline <- log(seq(3, 8, length.out = species))
block_effect <- matrix(rnorm(8 * species, sd = 0.2), 8, species)
cell_effect <- matrix(rnorm(16 * species, sd = 0.3), 16, species)
treatment_shift <- c(rep(0.25, species / 2), rep(-0.1, species / 2))

linear_predictor <- matrix(baseline, nrow(sampling), species, byrow = TRUE) +
  block_effect[sampling$block, ] + cell_effect[cell, ] +
  outer(as.numeric(sampling$treatment == "restored"), treatment_shift) +
  matrix(rnorm(nrow(sampling) * species, sd = 0.12), nrow(sampling), species)
community <- matrix(
  rpois(length(linear_predictor), lambda = exp(linear_predictor)),
  nrow(sampling), species
)
colnames(community) <- paste0("taxon", seq_len(species))
table(sampling$block, sampling$treatment)
#>    
#>     reference restored
#>   1         3        3
#>   2         3        3
#>   3         3        3
#>   4         3        3
#>   5         3        3
#>   6         3        3
#>   7         3        3
#>   8         3        3

    Declare the interaction covariance component

    The fixed treatment is crossed with block. Consequently, its null denominator is treatment-by-block variation, not residual quadrat variation. The random interaction must be written explicitly.

    bray <- vegan::vegdist(community, method = "bray")
design <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | block) + (1 | treatment:block),
  sampling, bray
)
design$random_term_table
#>              term      origin parent       variables      expression slope
#> 1           block        main   <NA>           block           block  <NA>
#> 2 treatment:block interaction   <NA> treatment:block treatment:block  <NA>
#>   correlated
#> 1      FALSE
#> 2      FALSE
design$spectral[c("euclidean", "negative_count", "negative_inertia")]
#> $euclidean
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $negative_count
#> [1] 23
#> 
#> $negative_inertia
#> [1] 0.5420573

    Permute complete cells within blocks

    Each treatment-by-block cell contains three quadrats. The permutation changes which treatment position receives a complete cell inside each block; all three quadrats move together. With two treatments in eight blocks, the exact space is 2^8 = 256 arrangements.

    fit <- permanova_crossed(
  design,
  p_method = "permutation",
  permutations = "all",
  seed = 20260718,
  truncate = TRUE
)
fit$table
#>        term df        ss        ms           denominator denominator_df
#> 1 treatment  1 0.2598841 0.2598841 1*MS[treatment:block]              7
#>   pseudo_f   p_value
#> 1 2.934605 0.0078125
fit$permutation
#> $algorithm
#> [1] "raw permutation of intact `treatment:block` cells within `block`"
#> 
#> $treatment
#> [1] "treatment"
#> 
#> $block
#> [1] "block"
#> 
#> $cell
#> [1] "treatment:block"
#> 
#> $treatments
#> [1] 2
#> 
#> $blocks
#> [1] 8
#> 
#> $replicates
#> [1] 3
#> 
#> $exact
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $attainable
#> [1] 256
#> 
#> $used
#> [1] 256
#> 
#> $seed
#> [1] 20260718
fit$tests$treatment[c(
  "exchangeable_units", "permutation_strata", "permutation_algorithm",
  "attainable_permutations", "exact_permutation", "approximation_status"

#> $exchangeable_units
#> [1] "treatment:block"
#> 
#> $permutation_strata

#> [1] "raw permutation of intact `treatment:block` cells within `block`"

    The empirical p-value uses the retained Gower matrix directly. It remains available if the Bray–Curtis spectrum has negative eigenvalues; no eigenvalue is discarded and no parametric F approximation is substituted.

    fit$tests$treatment$denominator
#> $expression
#> [1] "1*MS[treatment:block]"
#> 
#> $coefficients
#>           block treatment:block        Residual 
#>               0               1               0 
#> 
#> $ms
#> [1] 0.08855846
#> 
#> $df
#> [1] 7
#> 
#> $pooled_strata
#> [1] "treatment:block"
#> 
#> $assumptions
#> character(0)
fit$variance_components$unrestricted
#>        residual           block treatment:block 
#>     0.026560813     0.002014501     0.020665884
fit$variance_components$truncated
#>        residual           block treatment:block 
#>     0.026560813     0.002014501     0.020665884

    Know the boundary

    Omitting the random interaction removes the variance component required by the treatment denominator. The permutation engine rejects this model before calculating a p-value.

    omitted <- compile_permanova_design(
  ~ treatment + (1 | block), sampling, bray
)
conditionMessage(tryCatch(
  permanova_crossed(omitted, p_method = "permutation"),
  error = identity
))
#> [1] "Unmodelled fixed-by-random interaction covariance component(s): block:treatment. Declare (1 | block:treatment) or set `assume_additive = TRUE` to explicitly assume their variances are zero."

    The same explicit failure applies to incomplete or unequally replicated cells, one observation per cell, additional fixed or random factors, / nesting, and the additive opt-in. Those structures require different exchangeability rules; they are not approximated by unrestricted permutations.
